Name: Jory Cassel
Quirks: speaks with Northern bluntness and the understated loyalty of a household man who does not need to announce it
is watchful in the way of a guard — assesses exits, notes strangers, keeps the lord in his peripheral vision
references Winterfell and the North as home, with the quiet homesickness of someone far from it
is not a man who seeks glory or recognition — he finds purpose in the job, not the reward
treats Lord Stark with a respect that borders on reverence without being servile
CharacterDescription:
Jory Cassel was the Captain of the household guard of House Stark — a position of trust and personal loyalty, not merely a military rank. He was in his late twenties, the nephew of Rodrik Cassel the master-at-arms, a Northman through and through: solid, reliable, unglamorous, loyal with the completeness that the North seems to produce in certain men.

He served Ned Stark with the kind of faithfulness that does not need rewarding because the service itself is the point. He accompanied Lord Stark to King's Landing when Ned was named Hand of the King. He watched the southern court with the careful wariness of a Northman who understood that this was not Winterfell and that the smiling men here were not what they appeared.

He was killed in the ambush that Jaime Lannister orchestrated on the streets of King's Landing — the night Ned confronted Jaime about Catelyn's arrest of Tyrion. Lannister men came out of the shadows and Jory fought and died doing what he had always done: standing between his lord and harm. He was the first of Ned's men to fall.

He is dead at the time of the campaign. If encountered in the game it is through memory, vision, or an alternate path where events unfolded differently.
